A sales scheduling agreement is a sales contract that is created for one or more materials and outlines the overall expected quantity to be delivered over a specific period of time. The customer sends in sales scheduling agreement releases, referred to as delivery schedules, at regular intervals to release a quantity of the material. The business process variant includes self-billing where the invoice is created by the buyer and communicated to the seller.\</p>     \</div>    \</article>   \</main>  \</body> \</html> | MBP-545_001 | Market to Lead | Business Process |  |

| Mining | BPV-2445 | Variant | Lead to Cash for Sell from Stock (physical products, scheduling agreement, without warranty and recall) | \<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM "about:legacy-compat"> \<html lang="en-us">  \<head>   \<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=UTF-8">   \<meta charset="UTF-8">   \<meta name="copyright" content="(C) Copyright 2024">   \<meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT">   \<meta name="Business Process" content="2cefa2fde59d4e11bb80d2b6fc15304a">   \<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="commonltr.css">   \<title>Lead to Cash for Sell from Stock (physical products, scheduling agreement, without warranty and recall)\</title>  \</head>  \<body id="loio2b3affb6d6e744a19092a8fb693f5ee8">   \<main role="main">    \<article role="article" aria-labelledby="ariaid-title1">     \<div class="body conbody">      \<p class="p">Managing contracts, delivery and invoicing process based on a scheduling agreement. A sales scheduling agreement is a sales contract that is created for one or more materials and outlines the overall expected quantity to be delivered over a specific period of time. The customer sends in sales scheduling agreement releases, referred to as delivery schedules, at regular intervals to release a quantity of the material. The business process variant includes self-billing where the invoice is created by the buyer and communicated to the seller. product type, order size and shipping costs, recall or warranty claims aren't possible such as in the chemical industry. However, a claims process addresses quality concerns\</p>     \</div>    \</article>   \</main>  \</body> \</html> | MBP-540_002 | Plan to Optimize Marketing and Sales | Business Process |  |

| Utilities | BPV-2318 | Variant | Source to Pay for Field Service Materials and MRO Materials | \<!DOCTYPE html SYSTEM "about:legacy-compat"> \<html lang="en-us">  \<head>   \<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=UTF-8">   \<meta charset="UTF-8">   \<meta name="copyright" content="(C) Copyright 2024">   \<meta name="generator" content="DITA-OT">   \<meta name="Business Process" content="8f79cc70f60843068686dbd1130bf984">   \<link rel="stylesheet" type="text/css" href="commonltr.css">   \<title>Source to Pay for Field Service Materials and MRO Materials\</title>  \</head>  \<body id="loioc3f04cbfb6134999b6042cacb4f86146">   \<main role="main">    \<article role="article" aria-labelledby="ariaid-title1">     \<div class="body conbody">      \<p class="p">covering all activities related to the procurement of MRO (maintenance, repair, and operations) or field service materials or all kind of assets (like spares, electrical motors, compressors, mechanical seals, rotary motors etc.,). For MRO-intensive industries or field service businesses, the procurement of such materials is considered a part of their direct spend since it directly relates to the core business of the company. It including procurement, distribution and balancing. For example: a distribution company would buy energy for distribution. They do so with long-term contracts and on the spot market. Their SLAs (and regulators) oblige them to balance the energy in their networks to ensure electricity voltage doesn't drop/surge by more than 1%.
